# Nikhil Kumar — Personal Website

Nikhil Kumar is a Computer Science and Data Science student at GL Bajaj Institute of Technology and Management in Greater Noida, India (B.Tech 2023–2027). This website is a personal portfolio and an evolving home for projects, learning, and connection.

## Main topics
- Programming with Python, Java, C/C++, JavaScript, SQL, HTML/CSS, and R
- Application development with React, Node.js, Express, Next.js, FastAPI, and Flutter
- Machine learning and data tools including TensorFlow, OpenCV, Pandas, NumPy, XGBoost, and Power BI
- Software engineering and full-stack development
- AI / machine learning and computer vision
- Data analytics and football analytics
- C++ and competitive programming
- Learning through projects and technical exploration

## Selected projects
- GreenEye: CNN-based plant-disease image classification across multiple crop datasets; résumé-reported classification accuracy is 92%; application stack includes TensorFlow, FastAPI, TensorFlow Lite, OpenCV, MongoDB, React, and Flutter.
- Blogit: full-stack blogging platform with role-based authentication, session handling, authorization, 10+ REST APIs, MVC architecture, validation, pagination, and centralized error handling.
- FootyPundit: exploratory football analytics project using performance, workload and transfer-related data to estimate market value and injury risk, combining outputs in a Player Investment Index and exploring signals through Power BI.
- Psychoveda: an in-development psychology learning and counselling platform concept; not presented as production-ready.
- Masterin7ways: creative React/Vite website experiment; current public repository status should be verified before linking.

## Content notes
Project visuals are conceptual illustrations unless explicitly stated otherwise. The 92% GreenEye metric is reported for the project datasets and is not a general performance guarantee. The project directory is refreshed from public GitHub metadata when the source project runs/builds. Current-focus text should be treated as an editable snapshot that may become stale.
